title: Nucleus pressure vs axial compression, 5 lumbar segments (Brinckmann & Grootenboer 1991, via Dreischarf 2014)

quantity.name: IDP
quantity.definition: absolute intradiscal (nucleus) pressure vs axial compressive force; median and range (min-max) of 5 L4-L5 segments at 0, 300 and 1000 N, as re-plotted in Dreischarf 2014 Fig 2d

source.sample: 5 human cadaveric lumbar segments (L4-L5 per Dreischarf 2014: 'median relationship for fife L4-5 segments'); primary PDF not on disk

secondary_source.authors: Dreischarf M, Zander T, Shirazi-Adl A, Puttlitz CM, Adam CJ, Chen CS, Goel VK, Kiapour A, Kim YH, Labus KM, Little JP, Park WM, Wang YH, Wilke HJ, Rohlmann A, Schmidt H
secondary_source.where: Fig 2d (black dashed median line with markers; red ranges at 0, 300, 1000 N)

protocol.summary: Axial compression of single lumbar segments, nucleus pressure measured (primary protocol not restated in Dreischarf 2014). Dreischarf applied the compression to its L1-L5 FE models as a follower load and read the L4-L5 nucleus pressure.
how_to_simulate: Model the segment (disc with both vertebral bodies; or L1-L5 with a follower load as in Dreischarf 2014)
Apply axial compression 0-1000 N, no moment
Read nucleus pressure in the L4-L5 disc at 0, 300 and 1000 N
Compare with the 5-specimen range (min <= model <= max)
protocol.notes: Secondary data (re-plot); the level is L4-L5 according to Dreischarf 2014. The owner's Ghezelbash 2024 Fig 2d plots the same three points (0.30 [0.19, 0.47] MPa at 300 N, 0.95 [0.65, 1.40] at 1000 N) labelled as the L2-L3 comparison, and its bars are this specimen RANGE, not SD. Remus 2021 (not on disk) quotes Brinckmann & Grootenboer 1991 as 1.08 +/- 0.2 MPa (L2-L3) and 0.88 +/- 0.26 MPa (L4-L5) at 1000 N - cannot be checked without the primary. Same data also in fe_model_comparison.dreischarf2014.L4L5_invitro_idp_compression_secondary (shared sample, do not pool both). Fig 2 of the on-disk author version (QUT eprints) is one embedded bitmap of 552x415 px for all four panels (Fig 2b plot area 208x123 px: 13 px per Nm, 2.248 px per deg). The image was read at its native pixels (pdfimages, lossless PNG); rendering the page at >=300 dpi only up-samples this bitmap and adds no detail.

data.note: lower end of the range not resolvable (at or near 0)

extraction.from: Dreischarf 2014 Fig 2d (black markers = median, red bars = range)
extraction.check_notes: Re-read 2026-11-13 on the native bitmap: x frame cols 324 = 0 N, 532 = 1000 N (300 N at col 386); y row 350 = 0 MPa, 76 px/MPa (gridlines every 19 px = 0.25 MPa). Red bar at 300 N rows 315-335 -> 0.20-0.46 MPa, marker rows 325-328 -> 0.31; red bar at 1000 N rows 245-300 -> 0.66-1.38 MPa. Same as the earlier verified test (0.31 [0.20, 0.46], 0.94 [0.66, 1.38]). Owner targets fe.json 'comp.L2L3.idp_300N.fig2d' 0.3 [0.19, 0.47] and 'comp.L2L3.idp_1000N.fig2d' 0.95 [0.65, 1.4]: same values within 0.02 MPa, i.e. the owner re-plotted this Dreischarf range; the 'L2L3' label there is the owner's model level, not the specimens' level.

pass_rule.rule: min <= model <= max at 300 and 1000 N
